articles.title: (Some good news!) Treasuries rally as AI selloff drives flight to safety, 10-year yield at one-month low
articles.desc: Lower Treasury yields ease financing costs across the curve, offering some relief to rate-sensitive sectors and to the AI firms whose borrowing has worried investors. That makes the bond rally partly self-correcting for the very stress that triggered it. A softer dollar supports Asian currencies and
articles.content: Lower Treasury yields ease financing costs across the curve, offering some relief to rate-sensitive sectors and to the AI firms whose borrowing has worried investors. That makes the bond rally partly self-correcting for the very stress that triggered it. A softer dollar supports Asian currencies and commodities priced in dollars. Oil remains the main threat to the rally: with Brent heading for a fourth straight monthly gain, any escalation in the Iran conflict could quickly revive inflation fears and push yields back up. The BoJ decision later today is the next test, and a hawkish surprise could firm the yen against a softer dollar. --- Oil is higher: Vessel on fire in Strait of Hormuz after incident near Oman, cause "unknown" (LOL) Stocks slammed: Earnings bloodbath: Intel crashes over 22%, Amazon over 12%. What's coming next? $6bn stolen in a hack: Chainalysis estimates $5.9B stolen in suspected Binance hack, nearly 4 times Bybit But ... at least Treasuries are bouncing! --- The AI selloff finally gave bond investors something to cheer, though with oil still climbing and central banks still hawkish, the celebration may be brief. Summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to around 4.90% and the 30-year to about 5.26%, both one-month lows The rally was driven by safe-haven buying amid renewed selling in AI stocks after Alphabet, Amazon and Intel results Strategists noted that AI concerns lowered yields and softened the dollar, unlike energy-driven risk-off episodes The dollar index edged down to around 101.8 but is on track for a second straight monthly gain The yen held near 157.8 ahead of the BoJ, with about an 80% chance of a December hike priced ANZ’s Khoon Goh sees this week’s central bank pauses as temporary, with more hikes possible in 2027 US Treasuries rallied as a fresh wave of selling in artificial intelligence stocks sent investors in search of safety, Reuters reported on Friday. The rally pushed benchmark yields to their lowest levels in more than a month and weighed on the US dollar. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note fell to around 4.90%, while the 30-year yield dropped to about 5.26%, both at more than one-month lows. Bond yields move inversely to prices, so the declines reflect strong buying of US government debt. The rally was triggered by renewed concern over the cost of the AI boom. Results from Alphabet earlier in the week revived worries about AI spending and pulled broader stock markets lower. Disappointing results from Amazon and Intel after Thursday’s close added to the pressure. As equities sold off, safe-haven bonds became more attractive. Strategists noted that the pattern differed from recent bouts of market stress. An energy-driven risk-off episode would typically lift the dollar and push yields higher. This time, one Singapore-based strategist said, the US-focused AI concerns came with lower Treasury yields and a softer or subdued dollar. That suggests investors are treating the AI selloff as a US growth and earnings risk rather than an inflation shock. The lower yields weighed on the greenback. The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of major peers, edged down to around 101.8, although it remained on course for a second consecutive monthly gain. Elsewhere in currency markets, the yen was steady near 157.8 per dollar ahead of the Bank of Japan’s policy decision. The central bank is expected to hold rates at 1.25% with a hawkish tone, and markets are pricing about an 80% chance of a hike in December. The euro was flat near $1.12 after touching its lowest level since May 2025 in the previous session. The Australian dollar held around $0.70, on track for a 1.2% gain in October. The relief for bond markets may prove limited. The Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand all held rates steady this week, but have signalled their tightening cycles are not over, with energy prices near multi-month highs. Khoon Goh, head of Asia research at ANZ, described the current pauses as temporary. He said the risk heading into 2027 is that elevated inflation could bring even more hikes. Brent crude is on track for its fourth straight monthly gain, the longest run in more than two years. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.content: Rajiv Kamath Joins BlastX Consulting as Director of MarTech Engineering Enterprise MarTech and AI leader brings 20+ years of expertise in Adobe Experience Platform, CDPs, and journey orchestration to help clients get more value from their MarTech investments. /PRNewswire-PRWeb/ -- BlastX Consulting, a digital experience consultancy focused on delivering lasting impact and better outcomes from your CX investments, announced today that Rajiv Kamath has joined the firm as Director of MarTech Engineering. In this role, Rajiv will lead BlastX's MarTech capability, helping enterprise clients design, implement, and scale the customer data and journey orchestration programs at the center of their MarTech stacks. He focuses on helping clients get full value from the platforms they already own, including Adobe Experience Platform, Real-Time CDP, Adobe Journey Optimizer, and Customer Journey Analytics. "Our clients have made major investments in their MarTech stacks. Now they need those platforms working together and delivering value," said Brian McIntosh, Chief Consulting Officer at BlastX Consulting. "Rajiv has spent two decades building that infrastructure for some of the largest brands in the world. He brings deep Adobe expertise, broad platform range, and a clear view of how data, AI, and customer engagement connect." Rajiv joins BlastX Consulting from Merkle, a Dentsu company, where he spent nine years leading enterprise CDP and AI marketing programs. He has delivered 11 enterprise MarTech programs for Fortune 500 brands across telecom, healthcare, retail, financial services, and entertainment, at customer profile scales from 3 million to more than 200 million records. His work spans the full lifecycle, from requirements and architecture to data strategy, platform design, and delivery leadership across onshore and offshore teams. His expertise extends beyond the Adobe ecosystem to Treasure Data and Salesforce Data Cloud. He holds Adobe Certified Expert credentials in Real-Time CDP and Customer Journey Analytics, along with Treasure Data Expert certifications in CDP data management, AI/ML, and AI agents. He has also built AI accelerators using large language models that cut CDP implementation timelines from three to four weeks to two to four days. "Companies have spent years building their customer data foundations. The next step is making them intelligent," said Rajiv Kamath. "I was drawn to BlastX Consulting because the team is focused on outcomes clients can measure. I'm excited to help clients connect their data, platforms, and AI so every part of the stack pays off in better customer experiences." Rajiv will work closely with BlastX Consulting's Adobe, analytics, and customer experience consultants to help clients activate real-time personalization, orchestrate journeys across channels, and turn their MarTech investments into measurable business value. BlastX Consulting helps enterprise brands get more from their customer experience investments. We combine data, technology, and strategy to guide clients toward measurable, lasting impact. From smarter data and analytics to more connected journeys, our strategic consultants work as true partners, turning insight into action and experience into long-term value. articles.title: The best touchscreen MacBook is already on your desk
articles.desc: Macworld Apple rarely arrives first to the party, but it tends to deliver an innovative twist when it eventually catches up to its rivals. AirPods, Face ID, Apple Watch, even the iPhone Duo weren’t the first of their kind, but they stood out for their leaps in design and functionality. However, as t
articles.content: Macworld Apple rarely arrives first to the party, but it tends to deliver an innovative twist when it eventually catches up to its rivals. AirPods, Face ID, Apple Watch, even the iPhone Duo weren’t the first of their kind, but they stood out for their leaps in design and functionality. However, as the launch of Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro just proved, that’s not always the case. Commercial touchscreen laptops have been around for almost two decades. Despite that, standard models have remained the default for valid reasons, most notably due to their perfect ergonomics. Instead of perfecting the formula as it usually does, Apple distracted fans with a recycled favorite—slapping on a glowing logo that had been retired a decade ago. What makes the touchscreen MacBook especially baffling is how unnecessary it is. Apple already figured out the touchscreen setup back in 2019, and it’s been hiding in plain sight all these years. Sidecar attachment Sidecar was released as part of macOS Catalina in 2019. Billed as a way to expand your workspace, it essentially lets you use an iPad as an external wireless display for your Mac. Once it’s connected via AirPlay, you can drag Mac windows to your iPad’s screen and interact with them as you would on your Mac. Most controls were previously limited to Apple Pencil or mouse and keyboard input, but with macOS 27, you can use your fingers, too. There’s even a handy Sidebar on the iPad for common controls, like bringing up the on-screen keyboard or returning to the iPad’s Home screen, along with the Touch Bar that was previously included with certain MacBook models. Apple Unhinged design Steve Jobs famously opposed touchscreen laptops because “after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off.” When reading early rumors about the touchscreen MacBook, I had expected—or at least hoped—Apple would do something different by incorporating an innovative hinge mechanism. A convertible form factor would have allowed users to interact with the touchscreen horizontally and easily switch back to the traditional laptop mode whenever needed. Alas, that did not come to fruition. I acknowledge that we shouldn’t take everything Steve ever said as gospel because technology evolves, but many of his remarks still hold true today. The main issue with touchscreen laptops has never been weight or thickness, as some Apple execs recently suggested. At no point while using my MacBook does it feel natural for me to extend my arm and touch its display, and most people would probably relate. The new MacBook Pro is no different, and a sturdier hinge and lighter chassis don’t resolve the actual problem. Sidecar is a whole different story, however. My iPad is untethered from the MacBook’s keyboard, letting me flexibly touch its screen horizontally or otherwise. This allows me to utilize touch input on macOS when the need arises without straining my arm. It’s precisely the kind of innovation Apple is generally praised for, and we’ve already had it for years. Out of touch The MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR Display caters to professional creatives by letting them interact with macOS apps using their fingers. Yet, curiously, the machine is seemingly incompatible with many of these professional creatives’ go-to accessory: the Apple Pencil. This bars power users from taking advantage of precise interactions, pressure sensitivity, tilt detection, and all the other perks they cannot achieve with their fingers. Meanwhile, Sidecar on the iPad supports Apple Pencil input—not to mention that iPadOS can run many desktop-class creative suites natively. So, whether you’re Sidecar-ing or using the iPad independently, you get to unlock advanced creation controls and workflows that surpass what you can do with the new MacBook Pro. Beyond functionality, using an Apple Pencil minimizes fingerprints on your display, and creators know all too well how relevant that is. I’m far from being a professional photographer, but I’m constantly wiping down my 13-inch iPad Pro M4 before editing pictures because color correction and healing blemishes on the pixel level require that kind of clarity. Without Apple Pencil support, the new MacBook Pro’s display is going to get all smudgy as you attempt to get work done. Mac Duo Another advantage for using Sidecar as a separate wireless monitor for your Mac is having two sets of app windows open on each screen simultaneously to work on more complex tasks. Touch Bar enthusiasts will also be delighted to learn that the discontinued MacBook feature lives on through Sidecar. Non-MacBook Pro users, like those with a Mac mini/Studio, MacBook Air, or iMac, will especially appreciate being able to utilize the touchscreen without spending almost $3,000 on a new laptop—all thanks to Sidecar. In fact, it might be wiser to buy a Mac mini and an iPad Pro than a touchscreen MacBook Pro. Let’s break it down. An M5 Pro Mac mini ($1,699) combined with an iPad Pro M5 ($1,199) costs $2,898—a dollar less than the touchscreen MacBook Pro (M5 Pro)’s starting price. With this package, you’d be getting one of the most advanced tandem OLED panels on the market and two desktop-grade processors instead of one, not to mention Apple Pencil support and far greater versatility. Foundry Pick a side I’ve long depended on Sidecar with my MacBook Air, and—unlike the touchscreen MacBook Pro—it remains a prominent example of Apple’s classic “It just works” philosophy. The built-in feature requires absolutely no setup, cables, or technical literacy. Your Mac magically pairs to your nearby iPad and lets you mirror or extend the display wirelessly. That’s the epitome of touchscreen support on a laptop, even surpassing the highly advanced convertibles in terms of practicality and overall user experience. Ultimately, if touchscreen laptops were truly essential, they would’ve evolved meaningfully throughout the past years, and Apple wouldn’t have waited this long to release one. Professionals have been using standard laptops for decades just fine, and add-ons like Wacom graphics tablets continue to thrive among digital artists due to their precision and horizontal designs. Steve Jobs once said that people don’t know what they want until you show it to them. Apple already showed us the right way to do touch on a Mac with Sidecar, and it shouldn’t have caved to market pressure to build the wrong one.

articles.title: GSA left sensitive Google Drive files open to staff, contractors
articles.desc: Auditors have flagged similar security failures since 2014
articles.content: GSA left sensitive Google Drive files open to staff, contractors GSA left sensitive Google Drive files open to staff, contractors Auditors have flagged similar security failures since 2014 Google's Gemini 4 Carbon looks like a diamond in the rough Google struggling to make AI Mode searches pay Please state the nature of the medical emergency: Google is building a robot medic for NASA How Google fumbled the frontend with Angular 2 Big Red gets cozy with Google to offer TPUs to AI customers A major US federal agency has repeatedly left sensitive information in its Google Drive accessible to employees and contractors who had no legitimate business need to see it, and auditors aren’t happy. The General Services Administration (GSA), which handles contracting, procurement, property management, and other elements of basic operations for federal agencies, has faced repeated findings of inadequate protection for controlled unclassified information (CUI) since at least 2014, according to a from the agency’s Office of Inspector General. Again. Controlled unclassified information, in the US federal government's parlance, is information that isn't classified but requires protection or restrictions on its distribution under applicable laws, regulations, or government-wide policies. Access is generally limited to individuals with a legitimate government need to know. According to the OIG report, that can include things like physical security info for government buildings, personally identifiable information (PII) of government employees, and proprietary business information, all of which the GSA has left exposed. According to the report published this week, employees and contractors have approximately 2.5 million documents stored in GSA's Google Drive. “During a limited search of GSA’s Google Drive, we found 116 files containing CUI that were improperly shared with all GSA users,” the report notes. That’s a limited search, mind you, and the OIG has plenty of reason to believe there’s more than just that sitting open for anyone with access to the GSA’s Google Drive instance to sneak a look at. The OIG said that GSA is failing to properly manage the third-party tool it has in place to prevent data loss and detect CUI exposures, with annual reviews of search terms incomplete or undocumented, many relevant search terms not implemented, and a failure to enable an available optical character recognition feature that could help detect CUI in scanned documents. Additionally, the GSA was apparently “unaware of the tool’s file size limitation of 15 megabytes,” meaning that even if the GSA was properly using that tool, some large files would still be skipped. “We also found that GSA lacks: (1) an approval process for properly sharing sensitive information and (2) a standard naming convention that could more effectively prevent exposures of CUI in GSA’s Google Drive,” the OIG added. As for what was exposed … it’s not great. According to the audit, site plans for buildings in Washington, DC were part of the improperly access-controlled files, with data that includes entrances and screening techniques, as well as the location of sensitive areas, like gun lockers. A progressive collapse analysis that "describes the building’s collapse vulnerabilities, defense vulnerabilities, and critical failure locations” was also exposed. PII of government individuals was also exposed, including social security numbers, addresses, dates of birth, and contact information. Proprietary business information was also exposed, “including proprietary research and vendor proposals with technical and pricing information.” This might not have been publicly accessible, but it’s still a shocking lapse of data control, especially given that contractors with access to the GSA’s Google Drive could potentially view proprietary information belonging to competing vendors, giving them an unfair advantage if they used it. articles.title: Jitendra Singh calls for transformation via technology as ESTIC 2026 concludes
articles.desc: Minister of State for Science & Technology Jitendra Singh on Thursday emphasised the need to move beyond scientific discoveries towards their practical application, as the success of India's research and innovation ecosystem must increasingly be assessed through its tangible contributions to nationa
articles.content: Minister of State for Science & Technology Jitendra Singh on Thursday emphasised the need to move beyond scientific discoveries towards their practical application, as the success of India's research and innovation ecosystem must increasingly be assessed through its tangible contributions to national development. Addressing the valedictory session of the "Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave" (ESTIC), 2026, the minister called for "transformation through technology."Building on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of outcome-oriented science and technology, Jitendra Singh highlighted the importance of identifying clear, measurable targets for the next three years to assess the country's progress and strengthen its long-term scientific and technological capabilities. The session featured presentations on key recommendations emerging from ESTIC 2026, followed by the release of two landmark documents. The National Vision Document for ESTIC 2026 brings together the long-term science, technology and innovation priorities of 12 ministries and departments across 12 thematic areas aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047. The India: Science, Technology and Innovation Outlook 2026 provides a comprehensive, evidence-based account of India's evolving science, technology and innovation ecosystem, with quantifiable information intended to support policymaking and strengthen engagement with international partners. The STI Outlook is envisaged as a dynamic resource that will be updated annually. The Minister said that emerging areas of science and technology offer opportunities to accelerate India's technological progress and improve the quality of life of its citizens. Referring to developments in biotechnology, genomics and space research, he emphasised the need to anticipate future scientific requirements, including space medicine, as human space missions become more complex and prolonged. He also drew attention to the wider applications of nuclear science and technology, including nuclear medicine, and stressed that their potential extends well beyond energy and strategic applications to healthcare and other societal needs. Jitendra Singh further emphasised the strategic importance of ocean science and the blue economy in shaping India's future economic and geopolitical position, while calling for affordable and accessible nutrition to remain a national priority. He said that the discussions and recommendations emerging from ESTIC should contribute to a more integrated innovation ecosystem, with greater emphasis on developing technologies, facilitating their adoption and advancing India's scientific capabilities. Participants called for stronger collaboration between research laboratories and industry, common performance indicators for researchers and industrial partners, greater exploration of conventional materials for advanced applications, and capacity building in specialised manufacturing tools and technologies. The session also stressed the importance of translating indigenous research into solutions that generate measurable economic and societal benefits. The valedictory session reaffirmed ESTIC 2026's emphasis on strengthening India's science, technology and innovation ecosystem through coordinated action across ministries, scientific institutions, industry and academia. With its recommendations spanning advanced manufacturing, ocean science and maritime technologies, biotechnology, autonomous systems, robotics, agriculture and nutrition, the conclave provided a platform for identifying priority areas for future research, technological development and deployment. The discussions also reinforced the need to connect scientific excellence with industrial adoption, national priorities and societal needs.
